gaps.sentence: 'I saw him this morning,' she said on Monday afternoon. She said she had seen him ___ morning.
gaps.explanation: This morning, reported later the same day, becomes that morning.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll have finished by noon,' she promised. She promised she ___ finished by noon.
gaps.explanation: will have + past participle becomes would have + past participle.

gaps.sentence: 'You may leave early,' the manager said. The manager said we ___ leave early.
'I really must have that report by five,' the editor said. The editor ___ on having the report by five.
gaps.explanation: Insisting on a demand: insist on + -ing (or insist that + clause).

gaps.sentence: 'I've lost my keys,' she admitted. She admitted that she ___ her keys.
gaps.explanation: Present perfect backshifts to past perfect: have lost → had lost.

gaps.sentence: 'Shall I close the window?' he asked. He asked ___ close the window.
gaps.explanation: Shall I...? (offering) becomes if/whether he should... in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'You should apply for the grant,' he told me. He ___ me to apply for the grant.
gaps.explanation: Advice is reported as advise + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'It was me who ate the last biscuit,' the boy admitted. The boy ___ eating the last biscuit.
gaps.explanation: Admit takes a gerund (admit doing) or admit that + clause — never admit to do.
